title: App Definition
description: The single, versioned, validated contract that fully describes an application. The AI emits this document (never freeform code); the runtime, UI, and dev->prod promotion pipeline all consume it. Runtime-provided base fields (Id, CompanyId, AppId, CreatedAt/By, UpdatedAt/By, DeletedAt, RecordState) are implicit on every entity and MUST NOT be declared here — note the lifecycle base field is 'record_state' (active/archived), leaving the key 'status' free for a business field.

schemaVersion.description: Version of THIS App Definition schema the document targets.

key.description: Machine identifier for the app, unique within a company.

version.description: Semantic version of the app definition itself; bumped on every published change (drives dev->prod promotion).

weekStart.description: Which day begins a week, for `weekday()` and `week_of_year()` in computed expressions. Default 'monday' (ISO-8601), where Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7. CHANGING THIS RESTATES EXISTING FIGURES: every stored weekday and week number is recomputed on the next write to its row, so an app whose rows are not all rewritten will hold two conventions at once. Decide it when the app is created, not after it has data.

archetype.description: What kind of app this fundamentally is — the recurring shape of the work, not the industry. The domain pass classifies it; the design pass builds the app's signature working surface from it instead of defaulting to generic CRUD screens.

kind.description: The primary archetype: tracker (system of record: registries, inventory, assets), pipeline (records advance through stages toward win/close: CRM, deals, recruiting), approval (request -> review -> approve/reject: expenses, leave, procurement), scheduling (people/resources placed on time slots: shifts, bookings, appointments), assignment (distributing people/items across stations/teams/owners), ticketing (intake queue triaged to resolution: helpdesk, incidents), planning (work broken into tasks/phases toward a date: projects, events, sprints), catalog (browse offerings and request them: service catalog, asset library), analytics (metrics/reporting are the product), forms (users design forms at runtime and collect responses).

coreJob.description: One concrete sentence naming the app's single core job and the working surface a user opens it to do that job (e.g. 'Assign employees to station shifts week by week on a board').

plugins.description: First-party or custom plugins this app enables.

relations.description: To-many and many-to-many relationships. To-one relationships are expressed as 'reference' fields on the owning entity.

presentation.description: How the app appears in the platform launcher/home tile (control-plane surfaces read this).

pages.description: Optional layout: named pages composing views into tabs (drives navigation + grouping). Omit to let the runtime synthesize a sensible default from the views.

processes.description: State machines over an entity's role:'status' field: the named states records move through and the legal transitions between them (each optionally invoking a command). The runtime derives the status field's options from the states, enforces legal moves, and renders a process stepper on the record detail.

commands.description: Domain actions users invoke on a record (Approve, Assign, Escalate, Mark Paid) — beyond the built-in edit/delete. Each names its entity, where it appears, an optional guard, optional input fields, an optional confirmation, and the effects it runs. Commands are the manual path into the effect engine and the verbs that make an app feel purpose-built.

visibleWhen.description: Show this block only when the condition holds — evaluated CLIENT-SIDE against the scope chain, so it can read screen state ('{{state.mode}}'), the bound record/row, or the actor. Give `value` (an expression) plus one of `eq`/`neq`/`in`. This is how a day/week toggle swaps which grid renders, or approval controls show only while pending. Exactly one of eq/neq/in — with none the block is always visible.

value.description: An expression resolved against the scope chain, e.g. '{{state.mode}}' or '{{record.status}}'.

eq.description: Show when the resolved value equals this.

neq.description: Show when the resolved value does not equal this.

in.description: Show when the resolved value is one of these.

fieldPath.description: A field key on the current row, or ONE hop through a reference field to a field on its target ('shift.start_time' = the start time of the shift this assignment points at). The hop is what lets a row be keyed or labelled by a fact it does not itself carry — an assignment knows its shift, but the DATE lives on the shift. Exactly one hop; the hop must land on a plain value, not on another reference.

filter.description: One condition. Address the value with EITHER 'field' (a key on the row) OR 'path' (one hop through a reference) — exactly one of the two.

path.description: Filter on a field one relation away — 'shift.shift_date' filters assignments by the date of their shift. Use this instead of 'field' when the fact you are filtering on lives on the referenced record.

value.description: A literal, or a SCOPE TOKEN resolved when the block renders: '{{actor.id}}' (the signed-in user — this is how a view becomes personal: 'my tickets', not everyone's), '{{today}}', '{{record.<field>}}' (the detail record), '{{item.<field>}}' (the nearest enclosing repeat row), '{{state.<key>}}' (the page's screen state, e.g. a filter-bar facet), or '{{<name>.<field>}}' for any repeat that declared `as: <name>`. A cell in a grid names BOTH axes at once: value '{{row.id}}' on one filter and '{{col.date}}' on another. Ranges: 'between' takes the inclusive pair [lo, hi]; 'overlaps' the window [from, to]; 'in'/'notIn' a list. Clock tokens work in any of those slots: '{{today}}', '{{now}}', '{{today+7}}', '{{today-2w}}', '{{now-4h}}' (units d/w/h; no month unit).

optional.description: When true, this leaf is SKIPPED whenever its resolved value is empty — so a page facet ('all owners') drops out of the filter set instead of matching only rows with a blank value. Pair with a '{{state.<key>}}' value that an unset facet leaves empty.

endField.description: For 'overlaps' only: the field holding the END of this row's range. The row's range is [field, endField]; the value is the window [from, to].

displayField.description: Field key used as the human-readable label for a record.

imageField.description: Field key holding a PICTURE of the record - a company logo, a product shot, a venue photo. The peer of displayField: that one answers what a record is called, this one what it looks like. A 'url' or 'text' field holding an image URL. Wherever the record appears - its own header, a table cell, a reference to it from another app - it is drawn with this image, falling back to its initials on a stable colour when the field is empty. Declare it only when the field really is an image; anything else renders as a broken picture.

role.description: Marks the entity's part in an archetype. Forms archetype: 'formTemplate' = a form/survey; 'formField' = its questions (reference the template, carry an 'answerType' field); 'formResponse' = a submission (references the template); 'formAnswer' = one answer per question per response (references both, holds an 'answerValue').

kind.description: SURFACE intent — how this entity is presented, distinct from its data shape. Omit (default) for a normal 'collection' the user browses as a list (table/board/detail). Use 'config' for a LOOKUP/reference list other entities point at (territories, product types, categories, risk tiers, partner types): still a browsable, editable list, but it is app CONFIGURATION — the shell groups it under a single 'Configuration' area instead of giving it a top-level nav entry beside the app's real subjects. Use 'settings' for a SINGLETON configuration record: app-wide config/policy/preferences with exactly ONE record per app — the runtime shows it as a grouped FORM (never a table, never a 'New' action). The AI only declares this intent; the compiler derives the surface (and infers 'config' when omitted).

series.description: Declares this entity an ORDERED SERIES, which is what lets a computed field call prev(). Records are grouped by 'partition' and ordered by 'order', and every figure that carries from one row to the next — a running cash balance, an opening headcount, a closing stock level — is expressed as prev(field, seed) instead of being typed row by row. The runtime recomputes a whole partition in order after any change to it, so a value cannot be left stale by an edit further up the series.

partition.description: A reference field on THIS entity. Rows sharing its value form one series — the periods of one budget scenario, the months of one plan. prev() never reaches across partitions.

order.description: A numeric or date field on THIS entity giving the order within the partition. 'Previous' means the row immediately before this one by that field.

ownedBy.description: Marks this entity as SUBORDINATE to a parent — it only exists inside a parent record (comments, line items, subtasks, notes, answers, attachments: records nobody browses as a standalone list). Subordinate entities get NO top-level navigation, page, or table view; the runtime embeds them in the parent record's detail as a child-block. Omit for PRIMARY entities (the real destinations a user navigates to and browses). The runtime also infers this from relation shape when omitted.

via.description: The reference field on THIS entity that points to the parent.

as.description: Optional override for how the child renders in the parent detail. Omit to let the runtime choose by the child's field shape (comment-like -> feed, checkable -> checklist, money/quantity -> lineItems, else -> table).

unique.description: COMBINATIONS of fields no two records may share — the constraint a single-field `unique` cannot express. Use it when the thing that must be one-of-a-kind is a pair: one booking per (page, start time), one score per (student, exam), one line per (order, product). Each entry lists two or more field keys of THIS entity and becomes a real database constraint, so it holds even when two requests race — which is exactly when a check-before-write does not. Fields that must be unique on their own use `unique` on the field instead.

detail.description: Authored record-detail layout: a block tree rendered with record binding (kinds: hub, tiles, fields, child, tabs, section, columns). Authored by the design pass; when omitted the runtime synthesizes a default detail from field groups and child entities.

peek.description: Optional COMPACT record layout for the quick-look peek/side panel (a row or card's openDetail) — a short summary, not the full detail. Same block vocabulary as detail. When omitted the peek reuses detail.blocks. Keep it tight: an identity header, a few key facts, the primary actions, maybe a short recent-activity list.

form.description: Authored create/edit form layout (draft binding): sections of field groups. When omitted the runtime derives sections from field.group labels.

derived.description: Server-filled identity string, recomputed on every write and read-only everywhere — the string counterpart of 'computed', which only produces numbers and booleans. A CLOSED set of platform rules rather than an expression language: these exist to build keys a unique index can stand on, and a key a tenant could author is a key a tenant could break. 'companyDedupKey' = country + city + the legal name including its form, normalised for case, punctuation and German spelling (Müller = mueller); this is what makes 'the same company twice' a constraint rather than a hope. 'companyCode' = a readable handle for the same entity, built from the register number when research has found one and from the country and name until then. Never combine with default/initial/computed.

group.description: Optional label grouping this field with related fields into a section/tab on the record's detail page (e.g. 'Address', 'Payroll', 'Emergency Contact', 'Immigration'). Fields sharing a group render together; ungrouped fields form the Overview. Purely presentational — no referential meaning. Use 2-5 groups on entities with many fields so the detail reads as tabbed sections, not a flat wall of fields.

default.description: Must NOT be set on a process-governed field — the process's `initialState` is its default.

initial.description: Create-time value rules, evaluated top-to-bottom against the NEW record: the FIRST rule whose 'when' holds sets this field's initial value, overriding 'default'. The guard may hop ONE relation via 'path' (e.g. 'room.tier'), so a field's starting value can depend on a REFERENCED record — the runtime idiom for a cross-record condition. Example: a booking's status starts 'approved' when its room's tier is 'standard' but 'pending' otherwise, so standard rooms skip approval while premium ones require it. Applied server-side at insert; the field must not be one the user fills in.

when.description: A leaf guard on the new record: { field | path, operator, value }. Use 'path' ('<referenceField>.<targetField>') to test a referenced record's field.

value.description: The literal value to set when 'when' holds (must be a valid value for this field — e.g. one of a select's options).

treeAggregate.description: For a numeric field on a SELF-NESTING entity (tasks with subtasks): how the value aggregates over a row's subtree in tree surfaces. 'sum' renders a parent as `own (subtree total)` — 'Estimated 14 (40)'. Display-only (client-side); server rollups already count every row (a parent's own value covers only its OWN direct work, never its children's — totals are the plain sum of all rows). Only meaningful on integer/decimal/money fields; set it ONLY where summing is the business truth (effort, cost — never rates, percentages or scores).

computed.description: Server-calculated value: the field is read-only everywhere and recomputed on every write. EXACTLY ONE of 'expr' or 'rollup'. 'expr' is a typed expression over THIS record and may return a number or boolean; expression dependencies are evaluated in order and cycles are rejected. 'rollup' aggregates records that reference THIS record and remains numeric. Valid expression outputs are integer/decimal/money/boolean; rollups are integer/decimal/money. Never combine with required/default/initial/options or role:'status'.

expr.description: Typed expression over this record: arithmetic (+ - * /), numeric or date comparisons (< <= > >= == !=), boolean logic (and/or/not), true/false, parentheses. THE COMPLETE FUNCTION LIST, and there are no others: pow(base, exponent), min(a, b), max(a, b); prev(field) or prev(field, seed) inside an ordered series; the durations days_between(a, b), hours_between(a, b), minutes_between(a, b), whose two arguments are bare date/datetime field names and may be one of each; and the date parts weekday(d), week_of_year(d), month_of(d), day_of_month(d), day_of_year(d), year_of(d), hour_of(d), each taking one bare date/datetime field name and answering a number. weekday and week_of_year follow the app's `weekStart` (Monday by default, so Monday is 1 and Sunday is 7); hour_of needs a datetime, because a plain date has no time of day. THERE IS NO today() OR now(), deliberately: a computed field is worked out when its row is written and stored beside it, so a figure derived from the current time would be right on the day it saved and silently wrong every day after — ask that question in a filter or a report, which run when somebody looks. There is also no date CONSTRUCTION and no if/then, and a boolean is never a number, so min/max are the only way to clamp: a usage charge capped at a ceiling is min(raw_usage, cap), a balance floored at zero is max(0, balance). Field keys may reference other computed fields when the dependency graph is acyclic.

rollup.description: Aggregate over records of 'entity' whose 'via' reference points at this record — or, with 'match', at whatever this record points at. Add 'window' to include only rows whose date range covers this record.

entity.description: The entity being aggregated (a child or any entity referencing this one).

via.description: The reference field on 'entity' that points at THIS entity — or, when 'match' is set, at the record BOTH point at.

match.description: A reference field on THIS entity. When set, rows are aggregated when their 'via' equals this record's 'match' rather than this record's id — a SIBLING aggregation. Both must target the same entity. This is how a period sums the hiring lines of its own scenario: neither owns the other, they share a parent.

window.description: A declarative SUMIFS, in one of two directions — use exactly one. SPANNING ROWS: 'from'/'to' name the row's own date range and 'against' names a date on THIS record the range must cover — a hire being paid in this month. DATED ROWS: 'at' names the row's single date and 'within' names a range on THIS record it must fall inside — a funding round landing in the month it closes, a one-off fee in the month it is paid. Bounds may be DATES or NUMBERS as long as all of them agree -- 'the months this hire covers' and 'the first six periods' are the same question over different scales, and a growth rate that runs for six months should not have to be restated as calendar dates every time the plan start moves. An empty bound is always OPEN, never exclusive: an open-ended hire is still being paid, and a monthly cost with no dates typed runs for the whole plan.

from.description: Spanning rows: date or number field on the aggregated entity where the row starts counting. Empty on a row means it has always been running.

to.description: Spanning rows: date or number field on the aggregated entity where the row stops counting. Omit the property, or leave the field empty on a row, for open-ended.

against.description: Spanning rows: date or number field on THIS entity that the row's range must cover.

at.description: Dated rows: the single date or number field on the aggregated entity — the day the money moves. A row with no value lands in no bucket.

within.description: Dated rows: the range on THIS entity the row's 'at' value must fall inside. Give at least one bound.

from.description: Date or number field on THIS entity: the start of the bucket.

to.description: Date or number field on THIS entity: the end of the bucket.

field.description: The numeric field on 'entity' being aggregated. Required for sum/avg/min/max; omit for count.

filters.description: Optional leaf filters ({field, operator, value}) on the aggregated records — e.g. only lines of kind 'service', only claims with status 'approved'.

options.description: Allowed values for select/multiselect. REQUIRED unless a process governs this field: a process's states are its options (value/label/colour), and authoring both is an error — put each state's colour on `processes[].states[].color`.

phase.description: Lifecycle meaning of this option, for a role:'status' select WITHOUT a governing process (a process's states carry the phase instead): 'not_started', 'active', 'done', 'cancelled'. Drives the same renderer semantics as processes[].states[].phase.

scale.description: Decimal places. A DISPLAY contract as much as a storage one: a decimal without it prints every digit the arithmetic produced, so a computed ratio reads '0.7294117647058823' in a table cell.

unit.description: Short display suffix for an integer/decimal — '%' for a rate, 'x' for a multiple, ' kg' for a weight (include the leading space yourself when the unit is a word). Appended after the number everywhere the field is rendered. Money declares its unit with 'currency' instead, so this is invalid there.

prefix.description: Short display prefix shown INSIDE the input, before what the user types — the fixed part of a value that is not stored. 'cordango.com/book/' in front of a booking page's slug, 'INV-' in front of an invoice number. The counterpart of 'unit', and display-only in exactly the same way: the stored value never contains it, so changing it later cannot invalidate a single row. Use it whenever a value only makes sense as part of a longer string, instead of making people imagine the rest.

input.description: A richer control for entering this value, where a plain box would be unusable. The value's TYPE and storage are unchanged — this only says how somebody fills it in. 'timezone' = a searchable list of IANA zones for a 'text' field (nobody types 'Europe/Berlin' correctly, and a wrong zone silently shifts every time the field touches). 'slug' = the URL-safe part of an address: lowercases and strips as you type, and pairs with 'prefix' to show the part that is fixed. 'weeklyHours' = the opening-hours editor for a 'json' field — seven day rows with time ranges plus dated exceptions; the shape a booking page's availability, a shop's opening times or a helpdesk's staffed hours all have, and the alternative today is typing JSON into a one-line box.

targetEntity.description: For 'reference' fields: the entity key this points to (in the app named by targetApp, or this app if omitted).

targetApp.description: For cross-scope references: 'platform' for a canonical platform entity (person/department/group), or another app's key (cross-app, grant-gated). Omit for a local reference.

onDelete.description: For 'reference' fields: behavior when the target record is deleted.

optionsFilter.description: For 'reference' fields: which target records this field OFFERS as choices. Without it a picker lists every record of the target entity, which is wrong whenever the target is personal - 'which calendar?' must offer the signed-in user's calendars, not all fifty in the workspace, and a list of identically-named rows belonging to other people is unusable even when it is harmless. Use '{{actor.id}}' for the signed-in user. This narrows what may be CHOSEN, not what may be READ - it is a usability and correctness rule for pickers, not an access control. The value already on a record always stays visible even when the rule disagrees with it, because silently blanking a field somebody opened to read is not a fix. Leaves use 'field' (a key on the TARGET entity); 'path' is not available here.

role.description: Semantic role of the field. 'status' = the single 'select' field records move through as a process (drives kanban/timeline; at most one per entity). 'start'/'due' = the entity's semantic start/due date ('date'/'datetime' fields only, at most one of each per entity) — drives generic date affordances (late-start/due-soon/overdue colorization, scheduling surfaces). 'unconfirmed' = a 'json' field (at most one per entity) holding the list of field keys whose CURRENT value was written by the system rather than typed by a person — research, an import, an AI suggestion. The runtime removes a key the moment a human write includes it, and the detail marks those fields as unverified, so a value can be filled in automatically without ever passing itself off as checked. 'differs' = a 'json' field (at most one per entity) holding an OBJECT of field key to the value the system found, for fields a PERSON owns where the system's answer disagrees. The companion to 'unconfirmed' and the reason the system never has to choose: a field somebody filled in is never overwritten, and a machine that knows better says so beside the value instead of replacing it. Cleared on the same terms as 'unconfirmed' - a human write that touches the key means they have seen the disagreement and theirs stands.Forms archetype: 'order' = the integer that orders a formField's questions; 'answerType' = the select field on a formField holding the question type (yes_no/single_choice/multi_choice/scale/short_text/long_text/number/date); 'answerValue' = the json field on a formAnswer holding the submitted value; 'answerRequired' = the boolean field on a formField saying the question must be answered (without it 'required' is a browser-side courtesy the server never sees, which is fine until a stranger can post); 'answerOptions' = the json field on a formField holding the choices a single_choice/multi_choice question offers; 'respondentEmail' = the formField whose answer is the submitter's own email address, which is what a confirmation link can be sent to; 'confirmMode' = the text/select field on a formTemplate holding 'none' (the default, and what almost every public form should be - a submission is accepted as it arrives) or 'email', which holds the submission back until the submitter clicks a link sent to their own answer. Opt-in and rarely right: double opt-in is a mailing-list convention, not a form convention, and asking for it on a survey defeats anonymity. Worth it when a form FILES something a person then acts on and a wrong address would send that somewhere real. 'targetEntity' = the text field on a formTemplate naming the entity a submission CREATES (a helpdesk intake form creates a ticket); 'mapsTo' = the text field on a formField naming which field of that target entity the question fills (empty = the answer is kept on the response only). Public perimeter: 'publicShare' = a 'boolean' field (at most one per entity) that decides whether THIS RECORD is served to people with no account at all - the switch an author flips to publish a booking page or a form, and the only thing that makes a record public; 'publicToken' = the 'text' field (at most one per entity, and required alongside publicShare) holding that record's public ADDRESS. The token is the credential: it is generated with real entropy, never typed by a person, and read-only, because a memorable public address is a guessable one and guessing it is the whole attack. The two go together - a share flag with no token has no address to serve, and a token with no flag has no way to be turned off.

mapsTo.description: Forms archetype, formTemplate only: the field of the template's targetEntity that THIS field's value is copied into when a submission is projected. How a form declares its routing and defaults — 'default_assignee' with mapsTo 'assigned_to' means every ticket from this form starts assigned to whoever the form names. Generic: the engine copies, it does not know what a ticket is.

inverseField.description: For oneToMany: the reference field on the 'toEntity' that owns the FK.

category.description: Grouping for the launcher (e.g. Sales, HR).

tagline.description: One-line description shown on the tile.

formBlock.description: A form-layout node: 'section' (labeled group) or 'fields' (editable field keys, optionally in 2 columns). The runtime always drops system/readOnly/auto fields and hideOnCreate fields on create, regardless of the authored layout.

blockSource.description: Where a block's rows come from. Give EXACTLY ONE origin. 'entity' iterates records — the usual case. The other three iterate things that are NOT records, which is what makes a second axis possible: a grid needs its columns to be days or statuses, and those have no table. Without a non-record axis every surface collapses to a list of one collection.

dates.description: ORIGIN: a date range — the week/month axis of a planner or roster. Yields one item per step with { id, date (ISO), label, weekday, isWeekend, isToday }; read them as '{{<name>.date}}' etc. Bound it with 'to' or 'count'. Exactly one of 'to'/'count' — unbounded renders 366 columns.

to.description: ISO date, or a scope token. Omit when using 'count'.

count.description: How many steps (7 = a week of day columns).

options.description: ORIGIN: the declared choices of a select field — the lanes of a funnel or pipeline, without needing a table of stages. Yields { id, value, label, color }.

platform.description: ORIGIN: the tenant directory, which lives outside any app's entities — the pool of real people to staff a board with.

via.description: Shorthand for filtering to the bound record's children: the reference field on the source entity pointing at the enclosing record/row.

aggregate.description: For 'stat'/'chart' only — reduce the rows to a number, or group them for a chart.

field.description: Required for sum/avg/min/max; must be numeric for sum/avg.

groupBy.description: For 'chart': the select/reference/date field to group by, or 'month_of:<dateField>' for calendar-month buckets.

filterBar.description: A search + filter bar above a collection of rows that narrows them CLIENT-SIDE — a list you can actually find something in. `search` lists fields the free-text box matches (a reference field matches its RESOLVED name, so searching a person reference matches the person's name); `facets` lists select/reference fields rendered as filter dropdowns (Assignee, Status). One shared shape for every surface that takes a filter bar (repeat grids, tables, child tables).

search.description: Fields the free-text box matches (resolved names for references). Omit for no search box.

facets.description: Select/reference fields rendered as filter dropdowns (Assignee, Status, Priority).

blockSearch.description: Wires a board/table to a PAGE-LEVEL search box (a `filterbar` block) instead of the surface's own toolbar: `state` names the page `state` var the filterbar's search writes, so ONE query filters this surface live. `fields` names the field keys the query matches (a reference matches its resolved label); omit to match any value. One shared shape for the board and the list on a merged page.

state.description: The page `state` var key holding the query string (the filterbar's search writes it).

fields.description: Field keys the query matches against (references match by resolved label); omit to match any value on the row.

groupBy.description: Group a table's rows into labeled sections by a discrete field — the Asana-style sections of a task list. `field` is a 'select' (groups = its options, in option order) or a LOCAL 'reference' (groups = the referenced records, e.g. per-project task sections). In a TREE table only top-level rows are grouped; subtrees stay nested under their parent. One shared shape for every surface that groups rows.

field.description: The select or local reference field on the rows' entity whose values become the groups.

orderBy.description: For a reference `field`: the field on the REFERENCED entity that orders the groups (a section's 'order' integer). Invalid for a select — its options are already ordered.

ungroupedLabel.description: Heading for rows whose group value is empty. Default "(No section)".

showEmpty.description: Also render groups that currently have no rows (structure over brevity). Default false.

config.description: View-type-specific configuration (e.g. table.columns, kanban.groupByField, calendar.dateField, dashboard.widgets).

page.description: A named page that composes views into a layout. Becomes a navigation entry.

entity.description: Primary entity this page is about (used for context, e.g. the 'New' action).

detailFull.description: Open this page's records in the FULL-SCREEN detail (a workspace/profile) rather than the side quick-look panel. Use when the record's detail is a rich page in its own right (an employee profile, a project workspace).

group.description: Nav grouping. 'config' collapses this page into the shell's single 'Configuration' section instead of a top-level entry. The compiler stamps this for kind:'config'/'settings' entities — you do not need to author it.

state.description: Typed LOCAL screen state — working UI state that is NOT database data (a selected week, a view mode, a capacity filter). Each var is read as '{{state.<key>}}' in filters, date axes, `visibleWhen` and control blocks, and written by `control` blocks. Non-persistent, page-scoped. This is what lets a screen offer interactive criteria (pick a week, toggle day/week) instead of a fixed query.

navSource.description: Turn this page into DATA-DRIVEN navigation: the shell lists each record of `entity` as its own sidebar sub-entry (a workspace of things — projects, boards, teams, spaces — instead of one static page). Clicking a record opens ITS detail (author that detail as the record's workspace: a hub plus its scoped child surfaces). The page's own `entity` must match, and `labelField` names the record. Use for the small handful of top-level containers a user navigates BETWEEN, not for long transactional lists.

labelField.description: The field whose value labels each record in the nav.

sort.description: Optional field to order the nav entries by.

max.description: Cap the number of records shown in the nav (default 20).

default.description: Initial value: a literal, or the token '{{today}}' for a date.

options.description: For type 'enum': the allowed values a segmented control toggles between.

block.description: A layout node, DISCRIMINATED BY `kind`: each kind is its own closed shape (see the block_* definitions), so a property belonging to a different kind is rejected instead of silently ignored.

childType.description: How the child renders. Omit to let the runtime choose by field shape. 'cards' = dated items PUBLISHED ELSEWHERE — a title, a source, a date, an excerpt and a link out — where the point is to read the item rather than to edit the row; 'feed' is the opposite (own comments, with a composer). Default false.

newButton.description: Show a 'New <entity>' button above the list that opens the create form — for a page-level list that owns creating records. Default false.

filterBar.description: Always-visible search + facet dropdowns above the table — for lists long enough that finding a row matters.

search.description: Bind this list to a PAGE-LEVEL search box (a `filterbar` block) so one query drives both a board and this list on a merged page. Distinct from `filterBar`, which is this table's own toolbar.

groupBy.description: Group the table's rows into labeled sections by a discrete field.

orderField.description: The integer/decimal field on the source entity that carries the rows' MANUAL order. Rows sort by it (empty last, then load order). Omit for automatic ordering.

inlineEdit.description: Edit cells in place: selects/dates/numbers/people change on click (a process-governed status offers its LEGAL transitions and runs the real command); the first column still opens the record.

inlineCreate.description: Render an "Add …" row at the bottom that creates a record in place. A page-level table has no parent record, so the new row gets only what you type plus the group and order it landed in — anything the table FILTERS on is not set, so a row added under a filtered tab may not stay visible.

newDefaults.description: Field values a row typed into the inline add row starts with. Equality filters on this table's source are applied AUTOMATICALLY — a list filtered to `my_day eq true` gives a new row `my_day: true` without being told, the way a child gets its parent from `via`. State here only what a filter cannot imply: a comparison such as `due_on lte {{today}}` says which rows to SHOW, not what a new one should BE, so a Today list wants `{ "due_on": "{{today}}" }`. Relative tokens resolve. If a new row still would not match this table's own filters, the add row is hidden rather than creating something that disappears on the next load.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

startField.description: The date field a record's bar STARTS at. For kind 'calendar': the date field that places a record on the month grid.

endField.description: The date field a record ENDS at, inclusive. Without it a record occupies only its start day, which is right for a deadline and wrong for a meeting: a two-hour appointment collapses to a dot and a three-day trip disappears after day one. Set it whenever the records have a duration. Required for `range: 'day'` to draw anything with height.

range.description: The zoom this calendar opens at: 'day' (one column with an hour axis — a schedule), 'week' (one tall row), 'month' (the grid, the default) or 'year' (twelve mini-months). The reader toggles between them regardless. 'day' needs `startField` to be a 'datetime': a date alone has no time of day, so an hour axis would show one empty column.

timeAxis.description: The hours the day view shows, and how finely it rules them. Only read by `range: 'day'`. Defaults cover an ordinary working day rather than all 24 hours, because a schedule you have to scroll to reach 9am is a worse answer than one that clips the night.

allowCreate.description: Clicking empty space creates a record THERE — the day in a month grid, the half-hour in a day view — with the date fields already filled in. What everyone expects of a calendar, and off by default because a read-only calendar over records somebody else owns (an imported feed, a team's absences) should not offer to add to it.

quickAdd.description: What the quick-add dialog asks for beyond a title, when `allowCreate` is on. The title and the date/time row are always there and need no declaring — they come from the entity's displayField and this block's own `startField`/`endField`/`timeAxis`. Everything else is optional and hidden behind an 'Add …' row, so the dialog opens small and grows only where somebody asks it to. Without this the dialog collects a title and nothing else, which is not enough to schedule anything: the time cannot be corrected and nobody can be invited.

fields.description: Extra fields of the calendar's own entity to offer — a location, a meeting link, a description. Rendered with the same controls the full form uses. Keep it to the few that decide whether the entry is usable at a glance; the rest is what 'More options' is for.

children.description: Child records collected alongside the new record — guests on a meeting. Written AFTER the record itself, because a child needs its parent's id: the record is the transaction boundary, and a child that fails to save never un-books the entry somebody already watched save.

via.description: The reference field on the child that points back at the new record.

childType.description: How it is collected. Only 'chips' is compact enough for a quick dialog; the same value renders the same editor on the record's own panel, so guests are added the one way in both places.

labelField.description: The field whose value labels each bar/entry.

colorField.description: A select field whose OPTION COLOR fills each record's bar/entry (a 'type' field → vacation/sick/personal colours).

openDetail.description: Clicking a cell that HAS a record opens that record's detail in a panel overlay (its hub/process/tabs), with a link through to the full detail page — the way a calendar entry opens without leaving the grid. An empty cell still creates on edit; combine with `editable` (edit the one field inline) or use alone (read the value, click to open).

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

entity.description: The child entity key. For kind 'settings': the kind:'settings' singleton entity this page edits. For kind 'cell': the entity whose record the cell reads and writes (usually the join entity a grid renders). For kind 'form': the entity whose create/edit form renders inline here (its authored `entity.form` layout is reused).

via.description: The reference field on the child entity that points to the bound record's entity.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

fields.description: The field keys to render. For kinds 'table'/'split': the COLUMNS of the list. Omit to render all declared fields.

as.description: Publish the current item under this NAME for every descendant, however deeply nested — '{{staff.id}}', '{{day.date}}'. Without a name a block can only see its immediate parent row, so a cell can never know which COLUMN it is in, and a grid is impossible. Name both axes of a 2-D surface (e.g. `as: 'row'` on the outer repeat, `as: 'col'` on the inner) and the innermost repeat filters on both at once.

emptyText.description: What to show when there are no rows. An empty grid cell should say nothing at all ("").

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

entity.description: The entity whose records form the reporting tree (an employee/staff file).

manager.description: The reference field holding each record's PARENT link ('reports to'). A record's parent is the record whose `identity` equals this field's value — an employee's manager is a person id, matched to the manager-employee whose identity (person) equals it. A self-referential manager field is matched by record id instead. Records whose manager is empty (or points outside the set) are roots.

identity.description: The field whose value `manager` points at; defaults to the entity's displayField. For an employee file whose identity is a person reference, name that person field here.

subtitle.description: A field shown as the card's secondary line (a job title).

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

source.description: Where the cards come from — usually scoped to the bound record via `via` (a board of THIS project's tasks).

groupField.description: The select or reference field whose distinct values become the board COLUMNS. A status field makes a process board — dragging a card between columns runs the matching transition command (confirm/input show). A reference field (station/owner) makes an assignment board — dragging reassigns it.

cardFields.description: The fields shown on each card beneath its title. Omit to show the first couple of plain fields. A money field renders as the card's emphasized value, a person reference as an avatar, a date quietly in the footer, and a select as a chip — so keep the list short.

sumField.description: A money/number field summed per column and shown in the column header as 'Σ · count' (the pipeline funnel, Pipedrive-style). Computed from the currently visible cards, so it honors the board's filters + search.

search.description: Bind the board to a PAGE-LEVEL search box (a `filterbar` block) so one query filters both the board and a sibling list on a merged page.

newButton.description: Show a 'New <entity>' button above the board that opens the create form — for a page-level board that owns creating records. Default false.

openDetail.description: Clicking a card opens its detail in a panel overlay (its hub/tabs) with a link through to the full page, instead of navigating away.

interaction.description: 'interactive' (default) allows drag-to-move between columns; 'visualization' is read-only.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

source.description: Where the bars come from — one row per record, usually scoped to the bound record via `via` (this project's tasks). The visible date window is DERIVED from the data (earliest start to latest end).

startField.description: The date field a record's bar STARTS at.

endField.description: The date field a record's bar ENDS at (inclusive). Omit (or leave a record's value empty) for a single-day marker.

labelField.description: The field whose value labels each bar and its row in the left rail. Defaults to the entity's displayField.

colorField.description: A select field whose OPTION COLOR fills each bar (a status field → the phase colour).

milestones.description: Optional diamond markers laid over the timeline — a second source (usually the project's milestones) placed by a date field.

openDetail.description: Clicking a bar opens its detail in a panel overlay instead of navigating to the full detail page.

interaction.description: 'interactive' (default) lets a writer DRAG a bar to reschedule it (move the whole bar, or drag an edge to change the start/end) — gated on update access and editable date fields; 'visualization' is read-only.

block_history.description: The record's activity feed: who changed which field, from what to what, when. Fed by the runtime automatically — no entity, no fields and no authoring beyond placing the block. Record binding only (a detail page).

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length. Every column of a composed grid — header strip and body cells alike — must use the SAME width, or the two drift apart and the grid stops lining up.

block_answers.description: What the requester actually said: the questions and answers of the form submission this record came from, in the form's own order. For a record FILED BY a form (a ticket from an intake form) — put it near the top of the detail, because the answers are the request. Renders nothing for a record created by hand. Record binding only.

via.description: The reference field on THIS entity pointing at the formResponse entity. Omit and the single such field is used.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length.

block_intake.description: The front door: the forms someone can fill in, and the form itself once they pick one. This is how a person who may NOT create tickets still files one — submitting needs only the right to respond. Collection binding (a page). Pair it with a filter so retired forms stay off the list.

entity.description: The formTemplate entity to list. Omit and the app's single formTemplate entity is used.

filters.description: Which templates to offer — typically the active ones.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length.

block_externalEmbed.description: A REVIEWED third-party widget rendered inside a sandboxed frame, about the record you are looking at - a share-price chart on a listed company. Record binding only. Deliberately its own kind rather than a data block: nothing here reaches the entity store, nothing is cached and nothing is promoted onto the record; what it carries instead is a consent decision, because a third party's script running in front of a customer is a decision somebody must make rather than a default they inherit. The server resolves the block's provider and derives the subject from the record - the browser never names what to embed - and a tenant admin must approve the provider before anything renders.

key.description: Stable identity for this block, unique among the entity's record-bound blocks. The embed endpoint addresses the BLOCK by this key so a caller cannot choose a provider or a subject by editing a request - blocks are otherwise addressed by tree POSITION, and reordering a tab would silently repoint a live panel.

provider.description: Which reviewed embed to render. A closed set: each entry is code that has been read, with its own tenant approval flag, never tenant configuration - a provider decides the URL and the parameters, an admin decides only whether it is on.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length.

block_relatedApps.description: What the tenant's OTHER apps hold about the record you are looking at - the deals, invoices and tickets that point AT this company from apps it knows nothing about. Record binding only. Nothing is named here and nothing is configured: the server walks every built app in the workspace for reference fields targeting this record's entity, so an app earns its place on this page by referencing the record rather than by being authored in. Each app is re-checked against the reader's own grants, so this shows what THEY may see and never becomes a way around a permission.

empty.description: What to say when no other app references this record yet. Worth setting: the empty state is the common one in a new workspace, and 'nothing here' explains nothing.

width.description: Fixed width for a layout box: a named size ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'), a pixel number, or a CSS length.

when.description: Optional guard evaluated against the triggering record — the workflow's effects run only when it holds.

condition.description: A boolean guard, used by command.when, process transition.when and workflow.when. Exactly one of: an 'all' array (every child true), an 'any' array (at least one true), or a leaf comparison { field, operator, value }. Values may be literals or context tokens '{{currentUser.id}}' / '{{today}}' / '{{now}}'. A leaf addresses its value with either 'field' (the record's own) or 'path' (one hop through a reference).

value.description: A literal. Ranges: 'between' takes the inclusive pair [lo, hi]; 'overlaps' the window [from, to]; 'in'/'notIn' a list. Clock tokens work in any of those slots: '{{today}}', '{{now}}', '{{today+7}}', '{{today-2w}}', '{{now-4h}}' (units d/w/h; no month unit).

endField.description: For 'overlaps' only: the field holding the END of this row's range. The row's range is [field, endField]; the value is the window [from, to].

path.description: Guard on a field one relation away — 'room.requires_approval' tests the ROOM this booking points at. One hop, same-app references only.

effect.description:
One typed side effect, shared by command.effects and workflow.effects. 'updateRecord' writes fields on the triggering record (target 'self') or a referenced record; 'createRecord' inserts into an entity; 'notify' sends an in-app notification; 'email' sends mail; 'webhook' POSTs to an allow-listed URL. String values may contain template tokens: {{record.<field>}}, {{actor.id}}, {{actor.name}}, {{app.name}}, {{today}}, {{now}}.

DISCRIMINATED BY `type`: each type is its own closed shape, so a property belonging to another type (a `url` on a notify, an `entity` on an updateRecord) is an error rather than an ignored extra.

target.description: Which record to write. Defaults to 'self' (the record the command or workflow fired on); give { "field": "<a local reference field>" } to write the referenced record instead.

set.description: Field key -> a literal, a template string, or a pick block { "pick": { "entity": "...", "filters": [...], "sort": [{ "field": "...", "direction": "asc" }], "field": "id" } } which writes the first matching record (blanks sort first ascending, so somebody who has never had a turn comes up first). A pick that matches nothing leaves the field alone.

setIfEmpty.description: When true, only write the `set` fields that are currently BLANK on the target — a fill-once stamp. Use to record the FIRST time something happens (e.g. a ticket_message workflow that stamps the ticket's first_reply_at on the first reply, leaving it untouched on later replies).

set.description: Field key -> a literal, a template string, or a pick block { "pick": { "entity": "...", "filters": [...], "sort": [{ "field": "...", "direction": "asc" }], "field": "id" } } which writes the first matching record (blanks sort first ascending, so somebody who has never had a turn comes up first). A pick that matches nothing leaves the field alone.

effect_createForEach.description: One new record per row of a source set — a payslip per active employee, a checklist item per template line, a period per month of a plan. The generic 'prepare the rows' action, run from a command button or from a record.created workflow. It COPIES values rather than tracking them: a payslip must not change when that employee's salary changes next year, which is the opposite of what a rollup or a computed field does. Give it a 'key' and it is safe to run twice.

entity.description: The entity to insert into — one record per source row.

source.description: What to iterate: rows of another entity, or a generated date range. Exactly one of 'entity' or 'range'.

entity.description: Iterate the rows of this entity. Read once, before anything is written.

filters.description: Optional leaf filters on the source rows — only active employees, only the previous run's lines. Values may use {{record.*}} to refer to the triggering record.

range.description: Iterate a generated date range instead of records: {{source.index}} counts from 1 and {{source.date}} steps through the dates. This is how a plan gets its periods without anybody creating them.

from.description: First date. A literal or a template such as {{record.plan_start}}.

count.description: How many rows. A literal number or a template such as {{record.plan_months}}. Arithmetic is not available here — put the number on the parent as a field.

step.description: Interval between rows. Defaults to month.

key.description: The fields that IDENTIFY a produced row, making the effect safe to run twice: a row whose key already exists is updated instead of duplicated. ['payrun','employee'] means one payslip per employee per run however many times the button is pressed. Omit only when duplicates are genuinely wanted.

set.description: Field key -> a literal, a template, or a pick block. {{record.*}} is the triggering record, {{source.*}} is the row being iterated (or index/date for a range). A pick block { "pick": { "entity": "...", "sort": [{ "field": "...", "direction": "asc" }] } } writes the first matching record of another entity.

url.description: The https endpoint to call. The host must also be allow-listed at runtime; a non-https URL is refused there, so it is refused here.

effect_enrich.description: Queue a background research run for this record: look it up on the public web and file what is found ALONGSIDE what a person typed, never over it. The effect returns as soon as the job is queued — enrichment takes minutes and involves paid third-party calls, so it can never run inside the request that triggered it. Progress shows on the record itself (enr_state) and in its run history.

target.description: Which record to research. Only `self` today: enrichment is defined per record type, and pointing it at a referenced record would research the wrong subject.

kind.description: How much to do. `full` is the ordinary run and is refused inside the freshness window; `refresh` is the deliberate way past that window, for a record somebody has reason to believe has changed. There is no identity search in either - the domain is supplied, never matched.

command.description: A domain action a user invokes on a record. Runs its effects (and, if bound to a process transition, moves the record's state) after an optional guard, optional input, and optional confirmation.

entity.description: The entity whose records this command acts on.

placements.description: Where the command button appears. Defaults to the record header.

when.description: Optional guard — the command is enabled only when it holds of the record.

busy.description: Makes this a button with STATE. While `when` holds of the record, the button stays visible but is disabled and reads `label` — for a command that starts background work and takes longer than a page load. Without it a user presses a research button, sees the page unchanged, and presses it four more times; `command.when` is the wrong tool because it HIDES the button, and a control that vanishes on click is worse than one that does nothing. The condition reads the record, so it stays true across a reload until the work finishes.

label.description: What the button reads while it is busy, e.g. 'Researching…'.

input.description: Optional fields collected in a dialog before running; their values are written to the record.

effects.description: The side effects to run. May be empty ONLY when this command is bound to a process transition (the state change is the effect).

emits.description: Domain event names this command announces, e.g. ['deal.approved']. Every write already emits '<entity>.created|updated|deleted', and a command that moves a process state also emits '<entity>.<newState>' — so only declare this when the domain word differs from the state key. Other apps subscribe to these names.

process.description: A state machine over an entity's role:'status' field.

stateField.description: The role:'status' select field on the entity this process governs. Its options are derived from the states.

initialState.description: The state a new record ENTERS the process in. Either a state key, or conditional entry: { rules:[{when, state}], fallback } evaluated top-to-bottom at insert, first match wins. A rule's guard may hop ONE relation via `path` ('room.tier'), so entry can depend on a REFERENCED record — e.g. a booking starts 'approved' when its room's tier is 'standard' and 'pending' otherwise, so standard rooms skip approval. This is the ONLY way to make a governed field's starting value conditional; `field.initial` is not allowed on it.

when.description: A leaf guard on the new record: { field | path, operator, value }.

state.description: The state to enter when this guard holds.

fallback.description: The state to enter when no rule matches.

terminal.description: A final state with no outgoing transitions.

phase.description: Lifecycle meaning of this state, independent of its key: 'not_started' (work has not begun — a past start date renders as late), 'active' (in flight), 'done' (successfully complete — rows get the done affordance and due dates stop warning; distinct from 'terminal', a done state may still allow reopen), 'cancelled' (closed without completion). Drives generic renderer semantics; omit when none applies.

command.description: Command that performs this transition. Omit to let the compiler synthesize one.

to.description: Recipient: a template resolving to a person reference, or an email literal.

link.description: 'auto' to deep-link the record, or a URL.

to.description: Recipient: a template resolving to a person reference, or an email literal.

entity.description: Entity key, or '*' for all entities.

commands.description: Command keys (on this grant's entity) this role may invoke, or ['*'] for all of the entity's commands. Commands are deny-by-default: a role must be granted a command to run it. On the '*' (all-entities) grant, only ['*'] is allowed.
